callouts.label: Family and Culture
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents family and culture.
callouts.description: Families and cultures shape routines, meanings, knowledge, food, care, and support.
callouts.ap_tip: Influence is not the same as control. Avoid treating one cultural pattern as universal.

callouts.label: Peers
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents peers.
callouts.description: Peers can model norms, provide belonging, share information, or apply pressure.
callouts.ap_tip: Peer influence can be protective or harmful. Supportive groups make healthy choices more possible.

callouts.label: School
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents school.
callouts.description: School policies, curriculum, climate, meals, activity, care, and belonging affect health.
callouts.ap_tip: Resources and experiences are not equal across schools. Students can help improve school conditions.

callouts.label: Media
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents media.
callouts.description: Media shape attention, norms, emotion, identity, and perceived choices.
callouts.ap_tip: Algorithms and advertising have goals. Media literacy creates a pause for evaluation.

callouts.label: Healthcare
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents healthcare.
callouts.description: Care affects prevention, diagnosis, treatment, trust, and navigation.
callouts.ap_tip: Access depends on cost, location, language, culture, time, and policy. Quality includes respect and shared decisions.

callouts.label: Neighborhood
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents neighborhood.
callouts.description: Design, safety, housing, recreation, and social connection affect daily opportunity.
callouts.ap_tip: Place reflects investment and policy. Residents hold expertise about local needs.

callouts.label: Transportation
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents transportation.
callouts.description: Transportation determines which opportunities are reachable and at what cost in time and money.
callouts.ap_tip: Safe options support independence. Accessibility should include varied mobility.

callouts.label: Food Access
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents food access.
callouts.description: Price, availability, quality, culture, time, and transportation shape food choices.
callouts.ap_tip: Information alone cannot create missing access. Food sovereignty includes community power.

callouts.label: Policy
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents policy.
callouts.description: Rules and budgets shape products, environments, care, education, work, and safety.
callouts.ap_tip: Policy effects can differ across groups. Evidence and community voice should inform decisions.

callouts.label: Economic Resources
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents economic resources.
callouts.description: Income, wealth, work conditions, and time affect housing, food, care, rest, and stress.
callouts.ap_tip: Resources are distributed through systems. Economic supports can be health interventions.

callouts.label: Natural Environment
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents natural environment.
callouts.description: Air, water, heat, climate, green space, and hazards affect health.
callouts.ap_tip: Exposure is not evenly distributed. Prevention can require collective action.

callouts.label: Community Advocacy
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents community advocacy.
callouts.description: Organized community voice can identify priorities, build solutions, and shift power.
callouts.ap_tip: Participation should be accessible and compensated when possible. Partnership means sharing decisions.
